q-1120.name: Question 1
q-1120.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{log}_{7}⁡(x+1)}{2} & =1 \\ {log}_{7}⁡(x+1) & =2\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is $7,$ so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{7}⁡(x+1) & =2 \\ {7}^{{log}_{7}⁡(x+1)} & ={7}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${7}^{{log}_{7}⁡(x+1)}=x+1.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & ={7}^{2} \\ x+1 & =49 \\ x & =48.\end{aligned}
$$

q-1120.html:
Question 1
?

If log7⁡(x+1)2=1, then x=

a
49
b
13
c
50
d
8
e
48
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term:

log7⁡(x+1)2=1log7⁡(x+1)=2

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is 7, so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

log7⁡(x+1)=27log7⁡(x+1)=72

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get 7log7⁡(x+1)=x+1.

Therefore, x+1=72x+1=49x=48.

q-25135.name: Question 2
q-25135.worked_solution:
To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is $4,$ so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{4}⁡(3x-2) & =3 \\ {4}^{{log}_{4}⁡(3x-2)} & ={4}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${4}^{{log}_{4}⁡(3x-2)}=3x-2.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-2 & ={4}^{3} \\ 3x-2 & =64 \\ 3x & =66 \\ x & =22.\end{aligned}
$$

Find x such that log4⁡(3x−2)=3.

a
623
b
683
c
834
d
22
e
33
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is 4, so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

log4⁡(3x−2)=34log4⁡(3x−2)=43

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get 4log4⁡(3x−2)=3x−2.

Therefore, 3x−2=433x−2=643x=66x=22.

q-100626.name: Question 3
q-100626.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term:

$$
\begin{aligned}-16{log}_{7}⁡(x-128) & =-48 \\ {log}_{7}⁡(x-128) & =\frac{-48}{-16} \\ {log}_{7}⁡(x-128) & =3\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is $7,$ so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{7}⁡(x-128) & =3 \\ {7}^{{log}_{7}⁡(x-128)} & ={7}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${7}^{{log}_{7}⁡(x-128)}=x-128.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}x-128 & ={7}^{3} \\ x-128 & =343 \\ x & =471.\end{aligned}
$$
